messages:
maria-cs: Hey team — customer Foliage Health opened a Sev2: user not deprovisioning when removed from Okta group. They say the user remains active in our app and still has the 'owner' role. Can someone look? :frowning:

sam-sre: Noted. Do we have the Okta event payload or a trace from our SCIM sync logs?

maria-cs: I have the Okta audit event and our SCIM worker logs. Okta shows group.removeMember, user id 00u1abc, group externalId = gh-prod-owners. Our SCIM service logs the PATCH but returns 403 on the membership delta apply. Paste below:

```
Okta event: {
  "eventType": "group.user_membership.removed",
  "user": { "id": "00u1abc", "email": "tjensen@foliage.health" },
  "group": { "id": "00g9xyz", "displayName": "prod-owners", "externalId": "gh-prod-owners" }
}
\nSCIM worker log [2026-02-14T09:22:47Z]: PATCH /Groups/00g9xyz
payload: { "Operations": [ { "op": "remove", "path": "members[value eq \"00u1abc\"]" } ] }
response: 403 Forbidden { "error": "membership_protected", "message": "cannot remove last_owner" }
```
\ndevon-identity: Hmm "cannot remove last_owner" — that looks like our protection rule for group owners. I remember we added a guard to prevent removing the last user with owner=true. That guard should only apply to interactive UI actions, not SCIM-driven removals. Looks like the SCIM mapping uses the user attribute `owner` for membership metadata and we've been treating it as canonical.

kelly-ae: Customer is blocked — they want the user removed ASAP. Is there a quick workaround?

devon-identity: Short term: we can run an admin API call to force-remove the membership (bypass check). Longer term: we need to change the SCIM mapper so owner flag from Okta doesn't trigger our last_owner protection, or we should map owner metadata to a non-protecting role attribute.

sam-sre: Can you share the SCIM group payload that our service receives from Okta? Need to confirm which attribute is mapped as owner.

maria-cs: From their provisioning debug logs (Okta -> SCIM push):

```
Group PATCH sent by Okta:
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    { "op": "remove", "path": "members[value eq \"00u1abc\"]" }
  ]
}
\nBut when we query the group right after, SCIM returns:
{
  "id": "00g9xyz",
  "displayName": "prod-owners",
  "members": [ { "value": "00u1def", "display": "alice@...", "owner": true } ],
  "meta": { "externalId": "gh-prod-owners" }
}
```
\ndevon-identity: There's the clue — we had a custom mapper that copies Okta group attribute `owner` into the member object as a boolean. Our membership-protection logic checks member.owner === true and prevents removals if it would leave zero owners. But Okta intends "owner" to indicate role semantics, not a protection flag. SCIM should treat it as metadata only.

maria-cs: Is this customer-specific mapping? Could explain why we've not seen this at scale.

devon-identity: Yes, Foliage Health uses a custom Okta Group Profile mapping we onboarded last year. We added a mapper like `group.profile.owner -> members.owner`. That was meant for UI display. We didn't anticipate the protection behavior.

sam-sre: Proposed immediate remediation steps:
1) Run force-remove admin endpoint for tjensen@ to unblock (I can run).
2) Patch SCIM service to ignore `members.owner` from SCIM deltas for protection checks (deploy patch to identity service).
3) Backfill script to reconcile groups where Okta removed users but membership still present (remove stale members where Okta no longer has the user).

maria-cs: Customer ok with temporary force-remove as long as it's auditable.

devon-identity: I'll prepare a small fix: in identity-service we currently do: `if member.owner === true && group.current_owner_count <= 1 then throw` — I'll change to check `member.protection_flag === true` (internal only) and not honor `members.owner` coming from SCIM/Okta. That requires a one-line schema validation filter + unit test.

kelly-ae: ETA?

devon-identity: I'll patch and test locally now — should be able to deploy to staging in ~2 hours, production after signoff in ~4-6 hours. I'll also add a migration job to clear any `members.protection_flag` set via SCIM.
deploy-bot: Started rollout: identity-service/patch-ignore-scim-owner -> staging (build 2026.2.14-1453)

sam-sre: Maria, I'm going to do the force-remove now. Leaving a note for audit.

```
Admin API call:
DELETE /v1/admin/groups/00g9xyz/members/00u1abc?force=true
Response: 200 OK { "removed": true }
```

maria-cs: Customer confirmed user removed and access revoked. They're relieved. :pray:

devon-identity: Staging tests look good. Patch changes:
- ignore `members.owner` values from external SCIM payloads for protection logic
- add flag `protection_flag` only set via internal UI or admin API
- add unit test for last-owner-protection to require `protection_flag`

sam-sre: Plan to deploy to prod after 30m validation window in staging. Will also run reconciliation job to remove stale members.

devon-identity: Pushed to prod, monitoring metrics for group-change errors. deploy-bot: Completed rollout -> production (build 2026.2.14-1531).
deploy-bot: Post-deploy check: group-change-errors count down from 12/hr -> 1/hr (mostly unrelated flaps).

maria-cs: Customer confirmed everything's stable. They're asking for details about what changed so they can adjust their Okta mapping. Devon, can you send a short note I can forward?

devon-identity: Copyable note: "We updated how Redwood treats `members.owner` from SCIM. External attributes named `owner` will no longer be treated as a 'protected' flag that blocks removals. If you want membership protection, set an explicit admin-only flag via our Admin API or manage owners in-app. Recommended Okta configuration: map role labels to group.displayName or group.profile.roleName, not to members.owner. We'll email a migration snippet to help convert mappings."

kelly-ae: I'll follow up with customer and hand them the snippet. Also adding a runbook item: SCIM owner-mapping incident playbook.

maria-cs: Thanks all. Closing the thread once runbook + migration script PRs are in. :white_check_mark:
